    Proposition 2.1(1): a Hom–Ext inequality gives a brick quotient #

    Let M be a finite-dimensional nonsimple brick over an algebraically closed field and S a one-dimensional simple module. If only finitely many quotients M / L with L ≅ S occur up to isomorphism (Remark 2.2) and dim Ext¹(M, S) < dim Hom(S, M), then M has a brick quotient of dimension dim M - 1 (exists_brick_quotient).

    Step 1 differs from the manuscript (owner-approved cleaner route): instead of Chevalley's theorem and the fiber-dimension theorem, the loci of quotient classes are covered by polynomial images (kernel_polyCovered), and the covering lemma PolyCovered.finrank_le replaces the dimension count. It yields an embedding S → M whose quotient N satisfies dim End(N) + dim Hom(S, M) - 1 ≤ dim Hom(M, N), which is the inequality the manuscript extracts from equation (2.2). Step 2 follows the manuscript.

      Proposition 2.1(1). Over an algebraically closed field, let M be a finite-dimensional nonsimple brick and S a one-dimensional simple module such that only finitely many quotients M / L with L ≅ S occur up to isomorphism. If dim Ext¹(M, S) < dim Hom(S, M), then M has a brick quotient of dimension dim M - 1.
